strings.name: Alejandro Aravena
strings.summary: Aravena studied architecture at the Catholic University of Chile and led ELEMENTAL after founding his own practice. His designs use resident participation and incrementally expandable housing to address budget constraints, and he participated in post-earthquake urban reconstruction. He won the 2016 Pritzker Prize and directed that year’s Venice Architecture Biennale; in 2026 he shared Chile’s National Architecture Prize with Smiljan Radić.
